No new public links' (features/settings/sections/WorkspacePolicySection.tsx:461) also blocks workspace-only sharing; and where public sharing is on, each workspace link exists briefly as a public token before the PATCH.

title: A suspended or pending-deletion owner's content goes dark on public links but stays readable and runnable through invited and workspace links.

Actual: After suspension, invited viewers and workspace members can still open the owner's artifacts and chat snapshots and write to the app's shared storage.

title: Scheduled tasks and Code sessions keep working after the account loses the plan that includes them.
detail: Expected: When the plan no longer includes scheduled tasks or Code (trial expiry, downgrade, comp removed), runs and sandbox actions stop with an upgrade message, as Slack does per turn (slack-assistant-turn.ts:415). Actual: A Free account keeps every schedule running on cron, Run now, resume and event triggers, and keeps running agent turns, shell commands and commits in existing Code sessions.

title: The scheduled task limit counts completed, expired and paused tasks, not active ones.
detail: Expected: Only active (enabled) tasks count, as the feature is described, or the copy says the limit covers all saved tasks. Actual: A Basic user with three finished one-time tasks cannot create a fourth until deleting old ones, and the error says to delete or upgrade.

title: A schedule paused by its credit cap, or skipped by an access or secret-handling refusal, sends no notification.
detail: Expected: The user is told when a schedule pauses itself or keeps being refused, with the reason and a link. Actual: The schedule stops or skips silently; only last_error on the schedule page shows it.

title: Opening a pull request and deciding an approval skip the workspace Code policy that commit and turns enforce.
detail: Expected: Every action on a Code session passes the same access check, including the workspace 'code' feature. Actual: After an admin turns Code off, or billing goes read-only, a member can still open PRs and approve a paused step that continues the turn.

title: Named Code environments are stored but never used: no web UI, setup scripts never run, and secret variable values are never saved.
detail: Expected: A user picks a named environment for a session; its setup script runs and its variables are injected, values never returned. Actual: Environments can be created by API and listed on mobile, but sessions ignore them and there is no way to add variables.

title: Project memory and the upload route the phone and CLI use also accept only the project owner, so a fix to chat in shared projects alone leaves members without project memory and editors unable to add files outside the web.
detail: Expected: Every gate on a member's path in a shared project reads the sharing grant: read access for memory scope and chats, write access for adding files, on every client. Actual: Saving a memory in a shared project returns Project not found; a member's turn would use global memory in place of the project's; an editor's file upload from the CLI or phone is refused at presign.

title: The computer use monthly cap can never apply: the model-to-slot lookup returns an earlier slot, so no turn is ever counted as computer use.
detail: Expected: Turns that drive the screen are counted against computer_use_requests, so the Max soft cap of 1,000 and hard cap of 2,500 (model-catalog.ts:1344-1345) and the soft-cap warning work. Actual: No request is ever tagged computer_use: the count stays zero, the cap and computer_use_monthly_limit_reached never fire, and usage attribution never files a turn under computer use.

title: A click that starts a download runs without asking, and in side panel tasks it is not even watched against site rules.
detail: Expected: Every download the agent causes asks first, or the copy says that a click can save a file. Actual: Files land in the Downloads folder from an agent click with no prompt and, outside Desktop-driven runs, no domain check on the final URL.

title: Full access asks before dropdown changes, back, forward, reload and window resize, which Auto does without asking.
detail: Expected: Full access asks no more than Auto: at least the same non-crucial steps run without a prompt. Actual: Choosing the most permissive mode produces more approval cards than the default on forms with dropdowns and on multi-page flows.

title: Changing the approval mode while a browser task runs has no effect until the next task.
detail: Expected: Switching to Ask first mid-task makes the next action ask, or the control is locked while a task runs and says it applies to the next task. Actual: A user who switches from Full access or Auto to Ask first to rein in a running task sees the chip change but actions keep running unasked.

title: An error reading the Clerk session is turned into signed out, which cancels a running browser task and shows Sign in instead of the retry state.
detail: Expected: A read error (for example the origin-bound session error clerkAuth.ts:178-206 throws when the cookie watcher resets the client mid-read; offline or Clerk timeouts are a suspected trigger) shows the Retry state and leaves a running task alone; only a definitive no-session result signs the user out. Actual: A network blip during a panel refresh shows Sign in to chat and stops the browser task with an account-changed reason.

title: Recording can start on a blocked or unapproved site, shows the recording badge, then silently drops every step and asks the user to name an empty recording.
detail: Expected: Recording is offered only on an approved, unblocked site, or the user is told before recording that the site must be approved to replay. Actual: The page shows the recording badge on a blocked or unapproved site, the user performs the whole flow, and the shortcut has no steps with no reason given.

title: The organization's site blocklist stops AGI acting on a site but not reading it: page text from an org-blocked site can still be attached and sent to the cloud model.
detail: Expected: An admin-blocked origin is unreadable by every extension feature, as an enterprise blocklist is understood, or the policy offers a read capability that is enforced. Actual: Text from sites the organization blocked is sent to AGI Cloud whenever a user attaches or mentions them.

title: Organization site rules can only arrive through Chrome enterprise policy: the workspace copy the code reads is never written and no admin screen sets it.
detail: Expected: A workspace admin without Chrome device management can set allowed and blocked sites from Workspace policy and the extension syncs them, as the code comment says and as Claude and ChatGPT allow from their admin consoles. Actual: Only organizations that push Chrome policy to managed browsers can restrict sites; every other workspace has no site controls at all.

title: Stopping a turn during a multi-tool batch discards the results of tools that already finished and tells the model they were interrupted.
detail: Expected: Tools that completed before the stop keep their real results in history; only the running and unstarted calls are marked interrupted. Actual: If the model wrote a file or ran git commit and the user presses Esc/Ctrl-C during the next tool in the same batch, history says the first tool never finished.

title: Stopping a turn while an MCP tool runs never tells the MCP server to cancel, so the tool keeps running on the server.
detail: Expected: Esc/Ctrl-C during an MCP tools/call sends notifications/cancelled with the request id, as the MCP spec describes, and forgets the pending entry. Actual: The server keeps executing (sending a message, writing a record, running a long job) after the user stopped the turn.

title: The plain line mode has no Ctrl-C handling during a turn, so Ctrl-C cannot stop a turn cleanly and agent-started commands are not cleaned up.
detail: Expected: Ctrl-C stops the turn (as in the TUI and exec), kills the agent's process trees, reconciles and saves the session. Actual: Confirmed: nothing races the turn against Ctrl-C. Expected outcome (not run): the default SIGINT kills the CLI, the agent's setsid process groups are orphaned and the session ends on a lone prompt; if an earlier /image registered a tokio handler, Ctrl-C is instead ignored.

title: dontAsk mode still prompts whenever a terminal is attached and is shown and cycled as ordinary Chat in the full-screen view.
detail: Expected: dontAsk denies anything not pre-approved without asking, regardless of TTY, and the TUI shows it as its own mode. Actual: agi -p ... --permission-mode dontAsk in a terminal opens approval prompts and waits; in the TUI the mode reads 'Chat' and the overlay asks like Default.

title: Any message that mentions plan mode, including 'exit plan mode', switches the full-screen session into plan mode.
detail: Expected: Only an explicit request switches modes, and 'exit plan mode' leaves plan mode. Actual: 'exit plan mode' keeps or enters plan mode; questions such as 'how does plan mode work?' lock mutating tools until a plan is approved.

title: /install-github-app prints a hardcoded install link that skips the web's account-linking flow and then points users at /plugin.
detail: Expected: The command opens the web connect flow (the connectors page or /api/github/install/start) so the install links to the signed-in account. Actual: Confirmed: hardcoded slug and wrong next step. Likely (depends on the GitHub App setup URL and real slug, not visible here): the install is not linked or the link 404s.

title: Many lower layers still write with raw eprintln! while the full-screen view owns the terminal, corrupting the screen and losing the message.
detail: Expected: Every notice raised while the TUI is active goes through the notice queue into the transcript. Actual: Text is drawn over the frame at the cursor, letters splice into the transcript and the notice is not kept.

title: The HTTP and SSE MCP transports never send a cancel notice, not even when their own timeout fires.
detail: Expected: On timeout or user stop, the client posts notifications/cancelled for the request id, so the remote server can stop work. Actual: Remote servers keep running a call the CLI has given up on, and its late reply is discarded.

title: On Windows the CLI says agent commands run with full user rights, but it actually refuses every command until --no-sandbox is used in a trusted folder.
detail: Expected: The in-app message matches the behaviour: commands are refused until the user trusts the folder and runs --no-sandbox (or the message offers that path). Actual: Windows users read that commands will run, then every shell tool call fails.

title: /copy on Linux drops the clipboard object right after setting it, so the copied text usually vanishes before it can be pasted.
detail: Expected: The copied text stays pasteable on Linux (a Clipboard kept on the app, or a background thread with wait), with OSC 52 over SSH. Actual: On Linux desktops without a clipboard manager, paste returns nothing or the previous contents, after a success message.

title: Session memories are saved without secret redaction, and the fallback stores up to 2,000 characters of raw conversation that later sessions load into the prompt.
detail: Expected: Secrets are redacted before anything is written to memory, and the fallback never stores raw transcript text. Actual: A token or password pasted in chat can be written to the memory files and sent to the model in later sessions.

title: agi migrate claude reads files Claude Code does not use and copies hooks and settings to places the CLI never reads.
detail: Expected: Migration imports mcpServers from ~/.claude.json (user scope) and hooks from settings.json into the files the CLI loads. Actual: On a real Claude Code install the report shows no MCP servers, and imported hooks or settings never take effect.

title: agi mcp-server runs tools with confirmation off, which also skips the user's saved deny rules.
detail: Expected: Rules the user saved with /permissions deny still block a command whichever client asks for it. Actual: Any MCP client connected to agi mcp-server can run commands the user explicitly denied.

title: /init writes a fixed placeholder AGENTS.md instead of one based on the project.
detail: Expected: /init surveys the repository (build commands, layout, conventions) and drafts real instructions for the user to review. Actual: The project gets a placeholder file the agent then reads as instructions.

title: agi usage and /usage show credit meters to Free accounts, breaking the rule that Free usage screens show only Upgrade.
detail: Expected: Owner decision: Free usage screens show only Upgrade, never meters. A Free account sees its plan and an Upgrade line. Actual: A Free account that signs in to the CLI sees full meters and reset times.

title: /mobile and agi remote-control tell users to steer CLI sessions from AGI Mobile, which is unreleased and hides Remote Control in v1.
detail: Expected: With Remote Control hidden on the phone (owner decision), the CLI does not promote it; /mobile says the app is not released yet or is hidden. Actual: Users are sent to a store page that has no app and told to start a relay no phone can join.

title: On Linux the CLI treats any bwrap on PATH as a working sandbox, so where unprivileged user namespaces are restricted (Ubuntu 24.04 default AppArmor) doctor passes and every command fails.
detail: Expected: doctor probes bwrap once (for example bwrap --ro-bind / / true) and reports the AppArmor/userns cause with the fix; install.sh warns when bwrap is missing or unusable. Actual: Likely: agi doctor says the Linux sandbox is available, then run_command returns 'Sandbox unavailable (... bwrap ...)'.

title: The Stop hook runs only when the session quits, so a Stop hook brought over from Claude Code never runs at the end of a turn.
detail: Expected: Stop fires each time the agent finishes responding, and a blocking result makes the agent keep working, as in Claude Code and Codex. Actual: Stop fires once, at exit. A hook that runs tests, formats or sends a notification when the agent finishes a turn stays silent until the user quits, and can never send the agent back to work.

title: Managed require-signed-plugins accepts a publisher key the governed user adds
detail: Expected: When an administrator requires signed plugins, the set of trusted publishers comes from the managed file or the organization, and user-added keys do not satisfy it. Actual: A user under requireSigned with the override forbidden can add a key to their own config, sign a plugin and install it as Verified.

title: agi marketplace install skips the integrity gate that agi plugin install enforces
detail: Expected: Every command that puts a plugin on disk applies the same rule: a pinned hash, a verified signature or an explicit unsafe flag. Actual: The sibling command installs an unsigned, unpinned plugin from any git URL after a warning.

title: An ask rule on an MCP tool, including a locked managed one, does not prompt when the session skips approvals
detail: Expected: A rule that says ask forces a prompt for that MCP tool in every mode, as it does for built-in tools and as the leaders' ask rules do. Actual: In bypass mode an MCP tool under an ask rule runs with no prompt; agi mcp ask and a managed ask rule have no effect there.

title: Bypass permissions mode also skips the user's saved deny rules.
detail: Expected: A saved deny rule blocks the command in every mode. Claude Code documents this: a matching deny rule denies the call 'even in bypassPermissions mode' (leader-docs/2026-11-22/claude-code/docs_en_agent-sdk_permissions.md.md:30, :90), and ask rules still prompt there (:34). Actual: With --dangerously-skip-permissions or bypassPermissions, a denied command such as git push runs without a prompt or refusal. Only execution-policy Forbidden rules and the sandbox still apply.

title: The quit, restart-to-update and clear-cache prompts ignore a running computer-use run and cloud Work steps on this computer, so quitting mid-run stops it without asking, contrary to the claim.
detail: Expected: Quitting or restarting while computer use is active (phase active or paused) or a cloud task is using this computer names that work and asks first, as feature row 38 claims; keep-awake covers those runs. Actual: The app quits silently, killing the input helper mid-task; the hosted Work turn then fails its next device step.

title: Desktop Settings offers Remote Control phone pairing to paid users and tells them to choose Add device in the phone app, but the shipped phone app hides that control, so phone pairing is a dead end (the browser-link path is separate).
detail: Expected: While Remote Control is hidden in mobile v1 (owner decision), the desktop does not offer phone pairing, or says it is not available yet. Actual: A paid user can start Remote Control, a QR code and timer appear, and no released phone build can scan it.

title: The always-on Stop Agents shortcut and tray Stop All stop only local coding turns and pause the screen; a hosted chat or Work turn keeps running and keeps driving paired Chrome and file steps, while the app says Nothing to stop.
detail: Expected: The shortcut that claims to halt every agent ends or pauses all agent work touching this computer, including hosted turns' browser and file steps, and says what it stopped. Actual: Only screen control pauses; browser actions in Chrome and file steps from a running Work task continue.

title: The desktop shell builds no right-click menu, so Copy, Paste, Look Up, spelling suggestions, Copy Link and Save Image are likely unavailable by right-click in the window (read from code, not run).
detail: Expected: Right-clicking text, a link, an image or a text field shows the usual menu, as in the Claude and ChatGPT desktop apps and in the same page opened in a browser. Actual: By the code, right-click shows nothing in the main window, Quick Ask and detached windows; misspelled words would be underlined with no menu to correct them. Needs a run in a packaged build to confirm.

title: The server honors a workspace setting that forbids Skip approvals, but no route or console control can turn it on, so an admin cannot stop members running tools without approval.
detail: Expected: The workspace console has a switch (as Claude's disableBypassPermissionsMode and ChatGPT's allowed approval policies do) that writes the key the server already checks. Actual: The key can only be set by editing the database. Every member of every workspace can choose Skip approvals.

title: After one person logs out, a second account signed in on the same phone can never register for push notifications.
detail: Expected: Logging out frees the device so the next account that signs in on this phone gets push notifications. Actual: Account B's registration is refused on every attempt; the Notifications screen says the device could not be registered. Only the multi-account hand-over and switch paths use release=device, which deletes the row.

title: If the push clean-up fails at log-out (offline or timeout) it is not retried after a restart, so the logged-out account's pushes keep reaching the phone.
detail: Expected: A failed server clean-up is recorded and retried on next launch or when the network returns, like the Siri token revoke. Actual: Lock-screen notifications for the signed-out account (reply ready, scheduled results) keep arriving until that account signs in again on this device.

title: The Session timeout setting on the phone is never enforced on the phone; only the web app signs out after that idle time.
detail: Expected: Either the phone locks or signs out after the chosen idle time, or the row says it applies to the web app only. Actual: Choosing 15 min changes nothing on the phone; the mobile session stays signed in.

title: Android builds get push notifications only if the EAS environment holds GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON, which the release runbook marks optional.
detail: Expected: Production Android builds always carry FCM config, or the config refuses to build without it. Actual: Unknown: the EAS environment is not readable from the repository.

title: The phone's Reduce sensitive content switch is stored only on the device and is never synced with the account setting the server enforces.
detail: Expected: One account setting: the phone shows and changes the same value the server enforces on every surface. Actual: Turning it on in the phone filters only that phone's typed messages; web, desktop, schedules and Siri answers stay unfiltered. Turning it on on the web makes the server refuse phone chats (422 reduce_sensitive_content) while the phone switch shows Off.

title: A queued offline message that fails once on replay stays marked queued while the phone is online and is not retried until the network drops and returns.
detail: Expected: After a failed replay the queue retries on its backoff while online, and the bubble offers Send now or Retry. Actual: The message sits as 'queued' with no control, possibly for the whole session, and goes out unexpectedly later when the network flaps.

title: Reopening a chat while a message is still queued removes the queued bubble, so a later drop of that message is never shown.
detail: Expected: Queued rows survive a history reload until sent or failed, and a dropped message is always shown as failed with Retry. Actual: The queued bubble disappears on reload; if replay later exhausts its retries the message is lost without any notice.

title: The side menu's Recents does not move a chat to the top when it gets a new message, on the phone or from web.
detail: Expected: The chat you just used, or one continued on web, moves to the top of Recents, as in ChatGPT and Claude. Actual: Order stays as of the last list load; an active chat can sit low or fall outside the 30 shown.

title: The phone's file picker hides JSON, HTML, XML and notebook files that AGI Cloud accepts and the web composer offers.
detail: Expected: In Cloud the picker offers every type the attachment contract accepts, read from the shared contract. Actual: The Android MIME filter excludes .json, .html, .xml and .ipynb (iOS behaviour depends on UTType conformance, not verified). Separately, staging validation uses the Local parser list, not the contract: isAcceptableAttachment (attachmentValidation.ts:118-124) rejects an .ipynb shared in with its contract type, and accepts a .java or .sql file sent as application/octet-stream that api.uploadFile then refuses at send (services/api.ts:660 resolveChatAttachmentMimeType).

title: When the microphone is denied, live voice offers only Try again and never a way to Settings, so the user is stuck.
detail: Expected: A denied microphone shows an Open Settings action, like dictation and the camera do. Actual: Try again asks the OS again; after one denial iOS (and Android after 'don't ask again') returns denied without a prompt, so the same error comes back.

title: A new Cloud chat on the phone starts on a fixed model, not Auto, against the owner's Auto-by-default decision and web's default.
detail: Expected: New Cloud chats default to the Auto routing profile, as on web. Actual: Fresh installs, new accounts and fallbacks after a plan change land on one fixed model; Auto only if the user picks it.

title: The phone saves only the oldest 200 Cloud artifacts, so newer ones vanish from the gallery and search after a restart and never come back.
detail: Expected: The phone keeps the newest artifacts, or refetches what it drops. Actual: An account with more than 200 Cloud artifacts loses its newest ones from the Artifacts gallery, Library artifact filters and search after the app restarts, until each is edited again.

title: The Mode (push to talk), Speed and Pitch voice settings do nothing in the Cloud voice conversation people actually use.
detail: Expected: Settings that shape voice conversations either apply to live voice or say they apply only to on-device voice. Actual: Picking Push to talk ('Hold the orb to speak') leaves live voice hands-free; Speed and Pitch have no effect there.

title: A Code agent turn started from the phone is held open in one HTTP request and is aborted on the server when the phone drops it, unless durable turns are switched on.
detail: Expected: Locking the phone or switching apps mid-turn leaves the turn running; the session screen picks it up on return and a push says when it finishes. Actual: If the deployment runs inline turns, the turn stops when the phone sleeps; the app then shows 'Could not reach managed Code' and puts the goal back in the composer.

title: The Code session list shows at most the 100 most recently updated sessions with no paging, so search, Oldest first and older sessions miss everything beyond that.
detail: Expected: Older sessions are reachable by paging and search covers all sessions; Oldest first shows the oldest. Actual: Session 101 and older vanish from the phone; Oldest first shows the 100th newest; search cannot find older sessions.

title: The composer effort menu offers None, Minimal and xHigh, but the host drops those choices as malformed messages.
detail: Expected: Every level the menu offers is accepted and applied to the session. Actual: Picking None, Minimal or xHigh closes the menu and nothing changes; no error is shown.

title: The editor offers Remote Control and tells users to pair from the Mobile app, but pairing is turned off in mobile v1.
detail: Expected: While the phone side is hidden, the editor hides or labels Remote Control as not yet available. Actual: Users create a pairing code that no shipped app can scan, then the code expires.

title: On Windows the installer and walkthrough say to install the CLI in Git Bash or WSL, but a WSL install is invisible to a local Windows window.
detail: Expected: Windows guidance says Git Bash (or MSYS2) for a local window, and WSL only for a WSL remote window. Actual: Users who follow the WSL advice get 'The AGI CLI at agi was not found' after reload.

title: After a fallback (editor-only) sign-in, two VS Code windows can rotate the same refresh token at once; the server treats the second as a replay, ends the session and sends a compromise notice.
detail: Expected: Concurrent renewals from one device produce one rotation. Actual: The second window replays the old token; both windows lose the session and the user gets a false compromise alert.

title: When the browser does not open, the fallback sign-in tells the user to open the link and enter the code, then stops polling, so that code can never complete.
detail: Expected: Show the link and code and keep polling until approval, expiry or cancel. Actual: The user approves in the browser and nothing happens; the editor stays signed out.

title: Continue in the Cloud waits for the whole agent turn in one request, and a long turn is reported as 'the task did not start, another device already answered this one'.
detail: Expected: Return once the turn starts, offer Open session, and say 'still working' rather than failure. Actual: A notification spins for up to about 13 minutes, then an error with an unrelated reason while the work continues.

title: The site still labels the CLI 'Coming soon' everywhere except the install box, although signed v0.0.1 is published and the release feed serves it.
detail: Expected: Runbook step 10 (docs/runbooks/cli-release.md:304-306): mark the CLI released once a signed release installs, so every page, the pricing capability row and plugin install copy agree with the feed. Actual: The /cli eyebrow flips to 'Signed release published' client-side while the same page's metadata, CTAs and a dozen other pages say Coming soon; pricing hides 'Cloud in the CLI and VS Code'; plugin pages say 'Published for the CLI' instead of the install command.

title: The download page offers browser downloads of unsigned CLI archives with no install command, no signature check and no Gatekeeper or SmartScreen guidance.
detail: Expected: The download row shows the verified install command first (as /cli does), and any raw archive link says how to verify SHA256SUMS and what macOS and Windows will show. Actual: A user who clicks 'macOS' gets a quarantined unsigned binary Gatekeeper blocks, with no instruction, and installs bytes nothing verified.

title: Stream resume gives up after about one second and can only replay a turn the server has already finished, so a mid-answer drop ends as an error or a cut-off answer.
detail: Expected: A dropped reply keeps generating server side and the client reattaches when the network returns, as the feature map's 'Better' claim implies. Actual: Resume succeeds only if the server already wrote the turn within ~1 s of the drop; otherwise the turn fails. When it succeeds the answer is marked stopped, not complete.

title: A provider failure in the middle of an answer is shown as 'Response stopped', the same as the user pressing Stop, and the failure reason is dropped.
detail: Expected: The turn shows the 'interrupted' notice that exists for this case (turn-error-notice.ts:148-149) and keeps the error class for the failure banner. Actual: ChatMessageList shows 'Response stopped.' with Try again (1951-1957), as if the user stopped it; no reason, no reset time.

title: The client never notices a silent stream: the server sends a keepalive every 2 s, but the reader has no idle timeout, so a half-open connection leaves the answer 'generating' forever.
detail: Expected: No bytes (not even keepalives) for, say, 10 s triggers the reconnect path and a Reconnecting notice. Actual: Spinner and Stop button stay until the user stops the turn by hand.

title: Opening a search result for an older message in a long chat does nothing, because the transcript is virtualised and the jump looks only for elements already in the DOM.
detail: Expected: The chat scrolls to the matched message and flashes it, however far up it is. Actual: The chat opens at the bottom with no highlight; the URL keeps the highlight params and the composer's autofocus stays suppressed (7831).

title: The delete confirmation says a chat 'cannot be undone' although deleted chats sit in Recently deleted and can be restored for 30 days.
detail: Expected: Copy states the chat moves to Recently deleted for 30 days and that share links stop working; memory learned from it stays (as the bulk copy says). Actual: Copy says the delete is permanent and says nothing about memories or share links.

title: In a temporary chat, Pin message, thumbs up/down and both Branch actions are offered but fail, because the server holds no rows for that chat.
detail: Expected: These controls are hidden or disabled in a temporary chat, as Schedule, Save as skill and chat instructions already are. Actual: Clicking shows an error banner or a toast; the thumbs state flips and then reverts.

title: The reply-ready notification uses the Notification constructor, which Android Chrome rejects, and the call sits in a render effect with no try/catch.
detail: Expected: Reply-ready alerts go through the service worker registration, or the constructor call is guarded, on every browser. Actual: On Android Chrome the constructor throws TypeError; an error thrown in an effect reaches the conversation error boundary ('Chat could not be displayed').

title: On /chat, a failed Pin, Unpin, Move to project or Delete from the sidebar shows nothing, because those handlers skip the shared failure toast.
detail: Expected: Every row action that fails says so, as WebAppShell and Archive/Rename do. Actual: For any chat other than the open one the failure is dropped; for the open chat it surfaces as a turn failure notice under the transcript ('Failed to update conversation').

title: Pinning a chat that belongs to a project has no visible effect in the default sidebar view: Pinned excludes project chats and the project list ignores the pin.
detail: Expected: A pinned chat appears under Pinned (or at least first, with a pin marker, inside its project). Actual: The pin is saved but the chat stays where it was, buried in a collapsed project row.

title: Chats inside projects are plain links in the default sidebar view, with no row menu and no running, unread or Needs you markers.
detail: Expected: Project chats get the same SessionItem row (menu, status dots, aria-current) as other chats, as in both leaders' sidebars. Actual: No rename, pin, archive, delete or move from the sidebar for any chat in a project; a running task or one awaiting approval shows no marker.

title: Sidebar inline rename starts from the title the row had when it mounted, and blurring the field writes that stale text back as the chat's name.
detail: Expected: Rename always starts from the current title and has an accessible name. Actual: Opening Rename and clicking elsewhere silently renames the chat to an old title or an abandoned draft.

title: A paste of 10,000+ characters is swallowed in image mode, video mode or on a text-only free model: the text never reaches the box and 'Put it back' is not offered.
detail: Expected: When the file cannot be attached, the pasted text is inserted as text (or the notice offers to put it back). Actual: The paste disappears and the notice talks about images or Free Auto.

title: The composer's drop handler listens on the whole window, so files dropped on a project's Sources or Knowledge zone are also (or only) attached to the chat draft.
detail: Expected: Only drops aimed at the chat reach the composer; other drop zones keep their files. Actual: Dragging a source onto a project page shows 'Release to attach to your message'; a knowledge upload also lands in the chat draft.

title: 'Run this on a schedule' puts the user's whole prompt in the URL query string of /chat/schedules.
detail: Expected: The draft prompt passes through client state or sessionStorage, never the URL. Actual: Prompt text is stored in browser history and sent in request URLs (server and proxy logs); very long prompts risk URL length limits (not tested).

title: The ```map answer block loads one public OpenStreetMap tile straight from the browser, with no pins, a fixed zoom and no image consent.
detail: Expected: The map block uses the configured tile provider, plots each stop, fits the zoom, and respects image trust. Actual: A country-level tile with no pins; each view sends the locations' centroid and the page origin to OSM.

title: The SVG sanitizer strips every style attribute and <style> block from Mermaid output, so classDef/style colours are always lost and diagram parts the CSS does not cover likely render as black shapes.
detail: Expected: Every diagram type the model is told to use renders legibly; author colours survive (sanitized). Actual: Author colours dropped (confirmed); notes and bars probably black with dark text in light theme (not run).

title: The Deep Research cost estimate reads the picker's model, so on Auto (the default) it always says no estimate is available.
detail: Expected: The estimate uses the model the research run will actually use (the resolved route or the run's model), so Auto users see a figure. Actual: Users on Auto never see an estimate; users on a manual model see one priced on whatever the picker shows now, even for an older message's plan.

title: Start import stays enabled while Persistent memory is off (the default), so the whole import runs and then every fact is blocked at the end.
detail: Expected: With Persistent memory off, Start import is disabled with the same 'Turn on Persistent memory first' hint, or the dry run reports that nothing will be saved before the user copies the prompt into another assistant. Actual: A new user (memory off) copies the prompt into ChatGPT or Claude, pastes the answer, previews it, commits, and is told every fact was blocked.

title: Share project in the sidebar row menu only copies the project's own URL; it never opens the sharing dialog.
detail: Expected: Share project opens ProjectShareDialog (workspace audience, Can view or Can edit), the same as on the Projects page. Actual: The project is not shared; the copied link opens 'Project not found' for anyone except the owner and existing workspace grantees.

title: Delete chat confirmations say 'This cannot be undone' although chats can be restored for 30 days, and omit that share links and published artifacts are revoked for good.
detail: Expected: Per AGENTS.md section 9 the question names the real consequence: the chat moves to Recently deleted for 30 days, and its share links and published artifacts stop working permanently. Actual: Users are told the chat is gone for good (it is not) and are not told their links will break (they will).

title: The schedule form says tasks are swept every 15 minutes, but production runs the sweep once an hour.
detail: Expected: The form states the real cadence and minimum interval, and validation rejects intervals shorter than it. Actual: Users can choose every 15 minutes, and a 9:30 daily task starts at about 10:00.

title: A Code turn started on the web is also one held request, so closing or reloading the tab ends the turn when turns run inline.
detail: Expected: A cloud session keeps working after the tab closes, and the transcript is there on return. Actual: With inline turns and a host that reports the disconnect, leaving the page stops the turn. Same root cause as the phone finding at cloud-code-turn-transport.ts:142, on the surface most Code users are on.

title: Revoke-key confirmation says chats, files and memories become unreadable, but the workspace key seals only the audit-stream secret
detail: Expected: The question before an irreversible action names the real consequence (AGENTS.md section 9), and an encryption control does not claim to protect content it does not encrypt. Actual: An Enterprise owner is told the key protects chats, files and memories. Revoking it leaves that content readable by us exactly as before; only audit streaming to their SIEM stops.

title: CLI release notes are GitHub's monorepo-wide PR list, so agi, /release-notes and the site show desktop, web and dependency changes, and the summary leaks a raw bot link.
detail: Expected: CLI release notes describe CLI changes in user words. Actual: Users see unrelated internal PR titles (including one named 'Claude/quirky curie 6kgban') as the CLI's changes.

title: The release smoke never runs a tool command and never starts three of the six archives.
detail: Expected: Each published archive starts at least once in CI, and one approved command runs through the sandbox on each OS. Actual: Three archives ship unexecuted; no smoke executes a command.

title: Billing portal sessions use the Stripe dashboard's default configuration, so any plan switch the portal allows bypasses the server's purchase holds and upgrade flow.
detail: Expected: Plan changes only through /api/upgrade, which checks holds and access; the portal allows payment methods, invoices and cancel only. Actual: Unknown: depends on the live dashboard setting. If plan switching is on, a past subscriber can move to any priced tier while the account is scheduled for deletion or under dispute.

title: Starting and downloading a full data export needs no recent re-authentication, unlike delete account, password, email, 2FA and API keys.
detail: Expected: A bulk export of every chat and file asks for a fresh sign-in check, or delivers the link only by email. Actual: Any holder of a live session cookie can produce and download the whole archive.

title: The image route checks only the plan-level image capability, never the image model's own catalog plan floor (tierPolicy.minTier).
detail: Expected: A per-model floor in the catalog is enforced by the route that serves the model, as chat does with checkModelTierAccess. Actual: A future image model marked Max-only would be served to Pro; the Basic floor on flash-lite is unreachable because Basic has no image capability.

title: Duplicating a project copies every source without a storage check, so a copy can push the account past its file storage limit.
detail: Expected: Duplicate refuses with the file storage message when the copied bytes would exceed the plan limit, or copies are not counted twice since they share storage_uri. Actual: A Free user at 400 MB of 500 MB who duplicates a 300 MB project ends at 700 MB; later uploads anywhere are refused until they delete files.

title: A failed attempt that will be retried still sends a 'Scheduled task failed' push and email.
detail: Expected: Notify failure only after the last retry, or say a retry is scheduled. Actual: A task with 3 retries can send 4 failure notices for one occurrence, even if a retry succeeds.

title: Automatic and mention-triggered PR reviews have no Code plan check.
detail: Expected: If reviews are a Code feature, only plans with Code can turn them on and receive them. Actual: A Free user who installs the GitHub App can enable reviews and get up to 100 a month, charged to the Free allowance.

title: The PR review debounce and monthly cap treat a database error as zero reviews and proceed.
detail: Expected: A cost guard that cannot be read skips the review. Actual: During a database fault every push gets a full model review.

title: The 13 released connectors are not available to scheduled runs, Slack answers or custom agent turns.
detail: Expected: Documented product scope; listed so the comparison does not claim connectors for these surfaces. Actual: Only interactive chat can use released connectors.

title: An Isolated sandbox can still reach the whole AGI app hostname, while the option says commands cannot reach the internet.
detail: Expected: Isolated allows only the provider-proxy path (or a dedicated proxy hostname), and the copy says what stays reachable. Actual: Code in an Isolated sandbox can call any public endpoint on the app host.

title: Uploading files, discarding changes and the sandbox's provider proxy on a Code session also skip the workspace Code switch that turns and commit enforce.
detail: Expected: Every route that acts on a Code session passes 'code', so turning Code off for a workspace stops all of them at once. Actual: After an admin turns Code off, a member can still upload files into an existing session's sandbox, discard its changes, read its files, and a running sandbox keeps getting model calls through the provider proxy.

title: Signing a browser out from Sessions, or Log out of all devices, leaves that browser's push subscription active.
detail: Expected: Ending a browser's session remotely also stops notifications to that browser. Actual: A browser signed out from another device keeps showing run notifications (title and body) until its endpoint dies or it signs in and out locally.

title: Local scheduled shortcut replay has no way to be created: no extension page sends CREATE_SCHEDULED_TASK, so the alarm, replay and task-run code is unreachable.
detail: Expected: Either a user can schedule a recorded shortcut and it opens the recorded site to run, or the local scheduled-task code is removed and the feature map row is Missing. Actual: The feature does not exist for users; about 400 lines of background code, an alarm listener and tests maintain a path nothing reaches.

title: The content script asks the service worker for page access on every page load on every site, waking the worker for sites the user never approved.
detail: Expected: Unapproved pages cost nothing: the worker pushes PAGE_ACCESS_CHANGED to approved tabs, or the script is registered with chrome.scripting.registerContentScripts only for approved origins. Actual: Every navigation in the browser produces one runtime message and keeps the extension worker warm.

title: Deleting an account chat warns that it cannot be recovered, but the server moves it to Recently deleted for 30 days.
detail: Expected: The confirmation says the chat moves to Recently deleted on the web for 30 days, matching the other surfaces. Actual: Users are told the deletion is permanent when it is not, and the panel offers no way to reach Recently deleted.

title: The worker's WEBMCP_DISCOVER_TOOLS and WEBMCP_CALL_TOOL runtime handlers have no sender and call a page tool with no approval or origin check.
detail: Expected: No unreachable handler that can invoke a site's write tool without the approval the agent loop requires. Actual: Dead, ungated code path kept alive behind the extension-page-only gate.

title: Approval history on the extension's Permissions page never shows the extension's own browser approvals or site access choices.
detail: Expected: A history placed beside Approved sites lists what was allowed or declined in the browser, as Claude's permission history does, or its label says it covers chat tool requests only. Actual: A user who approved clicks, uploads and site access all day sees none of it there; the list holds unrelated cloud tool decisions from any device.

title: On banking, health, sign-in and password-manager sites the every-step approval skips console and network reads.
detail: Expected: On a sensitive site every read as well as every action asks, including the list of network request addresses and console messages. Actual: During an approved run on a bank or identity-provider page the agent can read the tab's console and its network request addresses, methods and statuses with no prompt.

title: Listing sessions panics when a session id contains non-ASCII letters, crashing the full-screen view.
detail: Expected: Short ids are cut on character boundaries (chars().take(8)) or ids are limited to ASCII. Actual: /history or /resume in the TUI, agi session list and agi history search panic for such an id.

title: Several registered commands only print text although their registry descriptions promise an action.
detail: Expected: Each description matches what the handler does, or the handler performs the action. Actual: Users run the command and nothing changes.

title: Full-screen /help omits the TUI-only commands, and some commands appear in neither /help nor the / popup.
detail: Expected: Every dispatched command is listed in /help and the popup, and the two interfaces accept the same names. Actual: Users cannot discover /worktree or /connectors from inside the app; /approve behaves differently by mode.

title: Messages queued during a turn are joined into one, so a queued slash command is rejected or sent to the model as text.
detail: Expected: Queued items run in order, each through slash dispatch. Actual: Queued commands do not run.

title: Session files are replaced by rename without flushing the new data to disk first.
detail: Expected: The temp file is fsynced before rename (and the directory after), as the conflict copy already does. Actual: Durability depends on the filesystem; on a crash shortly after a save the file can be empty.

title: The /ultrareview prompt sent for customers names a file that exists only in our own repository.
detail: Expected: The prompt is self-contained or ships the taxonomy with the CLI. Actual: The model looks for a missing file in the user's project.

title: The command-coverage tests compare the registry to hand-written name lists, not to the dispatchers.
detail: Expected: The test dispatches each registered name through handle_slash/handle_slash_command and asserts it is not reported as unknown. Actual: The guard passes on an input it never exercises.

title: A session name given with -n/--name or /tag is never saved, so --resume <name> cannot find it.
detail: Expected: -n my-work titles the saved session, it shows in agi history and /resume, and agi --resume my-work reopens it. Actual: agi --resume my-work fails with 'Session my-work not found'; /tag reports 'Session tagged' and the tag is lost.

title: /rename needs the session id although it is listed as renaming the current session, and renaming the open session reads as another app's change.
detail: Expected: /rename <title> renames the current session in place. Actual: /rename New title answers with a usage error; with the id it works but triggers a misleading notice.

title: /insights does not dump the session's events; it prints a command that would run a new paid turn.
detail: Expected: /insights shows or writes the current session's recorded events. Actual: The only output is a command that costs a turn and shows only future events.

title: /debug toggles a flag that nothing reads while claiming verbose tool output and hook traces are on.
detail: Expected: Debug mode changes output (verbose tool output, hook traces) or the command is removed. Actual: Nothing changes.

title: Unreadable lines in a session file are skipped silently, and the next save tells the user another process wrote the session.
detail: Expected: Resuming a damaged session says how many records were skipped and where the original is kept. Actual: The user sees no notice at load and a false 'another agi process' notice at the first save.

title: Status line choices made in /statusline are lost on restart, unlike /title.
detail: Expected: The choice is saved per project like the title and theme. Actual: Every new session shows the default status line.

title: /skills remove permanently deletes the skill's whole folder without asking or using the Trash.
detail: Expected: Ask once, naming what is lost, and move the folder to the Trash. Actual: One command deletes the folder permanently.

title: Discarding a hunk in /diff-review reverse-applies it to the working tree with no recovery copy.
detail: Expected: Keep a recoverable copy (a stash entry or a saved patch) and say where it is. Actual: Uncommitted work in that hunk is gone.

title: /pr-comments and /autofix-pr run several gh calls synchronously on the full-screen view's thread with no timeout.
detail: Expected: The fetch runs as a deferred async action with a spinner, a timeout and Esc to cancel. Actual: On a slow network the TUI freezes; Ctrl-C does nothing because raw mode swallows SIGINT.

title: Memory extraction uses the session's own model, runs during the session and at exit, and can hold the exit for 30 seconds without saying why.
detail: Expected: A cheap model does extraction, and exit shows a short 'saving memory' notice or runs it in the background. Actual: Users on a top-tier model pay its price for every extraction and can see the terminal hang for up to 30 s after quitting.

title: agi review --post puts the PR diff in a plain code fence with no untrusted-data framing and posts unparseable model output verbatim under the user's account.
detail: Expected: The diff is framed as untrusted data with a delimiter it cannot close, and output that is not a valid review is not posted. Actual: A crafted PR can steer the text that the user's account posts as its review.

title: A ! command in the full-screen view is awaited inside the event loop, so the screen freezes until it finishes and Esc cannot stop it.
detail: Expected: The command runs with a live spinner and Esc stops it. Actual: The TUI stops responding for up to 30 s per command.

title: In the full-screen view, /history search matches only the picker label, not what was said in the sessions.
detail: Expected: /history search <words> finds sessions by their content, as agi history search does. Actual: Only title or date matches are found.

title: /attach cannot attach a file whose path contains a space.
detail: Expected: Quoted or unquoted paths with spaces attach (macOS screenshots have spaces by default). Actual: 'Could not attach Screen: ...'.

title: CLI usage output and limit messages tell paid users to 'Add credits' while top-up sales are closed until 2027-01-01.
detail: Expected: Owner decision: no subscription or top-up sales before 2027-01-01; copy does not offer a purchase that cannot be made. Actual: Users are sent to a billing page where credits cannot be bought.

title: Repository docs still say the CLI release has never shipped after v0.0.1 was published on 2026-11-21.
detail: Expected: Docs describe current reality (AGENTS.md section 11); runbook steps 10 and 11 done after the first release. Actual: Six documents contradict the published release.

title: agi update tells every install to run 'agi update --install', including Windows, Homebrew, cargo and desktop-bundled copies where --install refuses, and the Windows refusal points to WSL, which installs a separate Linux copy.
detail: Expected: agi update names the command that works for this install, as the startup notice does. Actual: Users are sent to a command that then refuses; Windows users following the WSL hint update a different binary.

title: The update check and post-update release notes run only in the full-screen TUI, so --plain, --no-tui, screen-reader and agi exec users are never told a newer release exists.
detail: Expected: Every interactive mode, including the screen-reader mode the CLI advertises, gets the update notice once. Actual: Line-mode and screen-reader users must run agi update themselves; /release-notes in the REPL never has notes.

title: The spend cap is described three ways: /budget says per turn, --max-budget-usd help says per session, and subagents and teammates count it against the whole session.
detail: Expected: One definition (per turn or per session) used by the loop, subagents, help text and /budget, in credits. Actual: A cap set with /budget can block subagents after earlier turns even though each turn is under it; the flag is in USD while the UI is in credits.

title: /insights does not show the session's event log; it prints a command that would start a new prompt in the session.
detail: Expected: As described in the feature map, /insights shows the session's recorded events, or the help says what it does. Actual: Running the printed command sends a new prompt and spends credits.

title: The feature map and README say the CLI source is not published, but the GitHub repository that hosts the releases is public.
detail: Expected: Docs state the real visibility and licence terms of the public repository. Actual: The comparison row and README understate what is public.

title: agi marketplace install --scope records a label and changes nothing
detail: Expected: project or local scope enables the plugin for that project only, or the option is not offered. Actual: Every scope value installs the plugin for the user everywhere.

title: A terminal turn in a cloud project names the hosted conversation but no message ids, so the server never saves the answer and the account copy depends on the terminal's own push after the reply.
detail: Expected: As the app-server, web, desktop and extension do, the request names the user and assistant row ids so the server stores the turn itself. Actual: If the terminal exits or loses the network before its push, the account's history has no answer for a turn that was generated and charged; every such turn also writes a server warning.

title: A folder's link to an account project survives agi logout and there is no unlink command, so the next account's Cloud turns in that folder send the previous account's project id.
detail: Expected: Signing out, or signing in as a different account, drops the folder's project link, and a user can unlink a folder. Actual: The second account gets 'This turn runs without your project's knowledge files: the conversation could not be filed under the project' on Cloud turns in that folder until it links some other project. No data crosses accounts because the server rejects the id.

title: When Quick Ask is redirected to an in-progress auth step (/login/complete for new terms or age review, /login/verify for account security), the panel hides and the main window is raised on its old page without going there.
detail: Expected: The step the panel was sent to (accept updated terms, confirm age, verify the account) opens in the main window. Actual: The panel flashes and vanishes on every shortcut press; the main window comes forward on whatever it showed, with no prompt explaining why Quick Ask will not open.

title: Chat-finished and update-ready notifications are created without keeping a reference, so on macOS a collected Notification may vanish from Notification Center and its click or Relaunch action may never reach the app.
detail: Expected: Clicking a chat-finished notification opens that conversation, and Relaunch to update installs, however long the notification sat in Notification Center. Actual: Not reproduced here: after a garbage collection the listeners may be gone and the notification removed.

title: On the desktop sign-in failure page, Sign in here instead only redraws the shell's Continue in browser screen, and the retry button gives no feedback.
detail: Expected: Labels match what happens: one Continue in your browser action that shows a waiting state. Actual: A link promising an in-app sign-in that does not exist, and a silent retry.

title: Settings' update row offers Download installer while the native updater is starting its download, and never says when the automatic download failed.
detail: Expected: Checking or downloading reads as downloading with no installer button; a failed download says so and offers the installer. Actual: Users are invited to download and drag in a DMG by hand while the app is about to update itself, and a failed automatic update looks the same as a fresh one.

title: Screenshot to Chat and Window to Chat put back only plain text afterwards, so an image, file or rich content the user had copied is wiped from the clipboard.
detail: Expected: The clipboard returns to what the user had, or is left as the capture, never emptied of their own content. Actual: A copied image or file is lost after one capture.

title: Security comments describe a shell that no longer exists: the entitlements say the app has no local files or automation, and the sign-in host list says a page reads it when none does.
detail: Expected: Comments that state current behavior (AGENTS.md section 2: prose contradicting code is a doc bug). Actual: Misleading guidance for anyone changing entitlements or the sign-in hosts.

title: The shell's Finish signing in in your browser screen never times out on screen after the 10-minute attempt expires.
detail: Expected: After the attempt expires the screen says so and offers Try again. Actual: The waiting screen stays until the user completes (then sees Sign-in link expired) or presses Open browser again.

title: View > Show Files and Edit > Find > Find in Files are always enabled but only a coding session on this computer listens for them, so in a chat or a cloud session they do nothing.
detail: Expected: The items are disabled, or hidden, when no session that has a file pane is open, the way Show Terminal is. Actual: Choosing either item in a normal chat or a cloud Code session has no visible effect.

title: On Android 8 to 12 the widget and app-icon Voice action silently opens the new-chat screen instead of voice mode.
detail: Expected: Voice opens voice mode or says why voice is unavailable on this Android version; or the control is not offered there. Actual: Tapping Voice lands on an empty new chat with no explanation.

title: On iPhone, content shared before onboarding or the age step is finished is not shown again until the next cold launch.
detail: Expected: A share that arrives before the app is ready is held and opened once the person reaches the app, like intent links. Actual: The share preview flashes or never appears; the shared text and files come back only after the app is killed and reopened.

title: A source comment claims Analyze Image and Scan register as Visual Intelligence actions automatically, which they do not.
detail: Expected: Comments state only true constraints (AGENTS.md section 9). Actual: The comment describes an integration that does not exist and could mislead release notes or review answers.

title: Many mobile screens hardcode https://agiworkforce.com instead of building links from the configured API origin.
detail: Expected: Paths such as '/privacy' resolved against API_URL, so preview and staging builds open their own web pages. Actual: A preview build pointed at a staging API still opens production legal, account and security pages.

title: The app handles https://agiworkforce.com/chat/<id> links, but neither the iOS association file nor the Android filters register /chat, so those links always open the browser.
detail: Expected: Either register /chat/* so chat links open the app, or drop the dead https branch. Actual: Only the custom scheme agiworkforce://chat/<id> can reach this code.

title: expo-sensors is linked and its config plugin registered, but no app code uses it.
detail: Expected: Unused native modules are removed (AGENTS.md section 9: no unused abstractions). Actual: An unused native module ships in both binaries and enters the fingerprint runtime version.

title: The diagnostics consent says it sends details to AGI Workforce, but the app only opens the system share sheet and the person chooses the recipient.
detail: Expected: Copy that says a file will be shared to the app the person picks (for example Mail to support), and a result that reflects a cancelled share. Actual: People believe support received the file when nothing was sent.

title: The Refresh button on the Usage page reloads only the meters; the month, storage, usage credits and history cards stay stale.
detail: Expected: Refresh reloads every figure on the page. Actual: After Refresh the 'This month' allowance, storage use, credit balance and history keep their first-load values.

title: Every settings switch puts On or Off in its label, so screen readers announce the state twice.
detail: Expected: Label is the name only; the switch role and checked state carry the value. Actual: Doubled state on every switch in Settings; the row View label is also unused because the View is not marked accessible.

title: The Profile page has its own Log Out confirmation that names no account, omits the hand-over to the next account and skips the stale-account guard.
detail: Expected: One shared log-out confirmation used from every entry point. Actual: From Profile, a person with two accounts is told they log out of AGI Cloud but silently continues as the other account.

title: Ask from Siri sets no authentication policy, so it likely answers from a locked iPhone and bypasses App Lock.
detail: Expected: Siri asks for device unlock before running an action that spends the account's usage and writes to its history, at least while App Lock is on. Actual: Unverified on device: with Siri allowed on the lock screen, anyone holding the phone can likely ask questions as the owner.

title: Sending the same text twice in one chat while offline shows two queued bubbles but sends only one message.
detail: Expected: Either both messages are queued and sent, or the second send is refused with a visible reason. Actual: Two bubbles show; one message is sent and both bubbles vanish.

title: Deleting or archiving a chat leaves its offline-queued messages in the queue, and they are sent on reconnect.
detail: Expected: Removing a chat removes its queued messages. Actual: A request is sent for a deleted chat and an orphan row is created and pushed.

title: Connector app cards never show the app on the phone; every card says the app can't be displayed and dumps the raw tool result.
detail: Expected: The comparison marks this row Same; the app's UI should render in a sandbox as on web, or the row should be Partial. Actual: A warning plus raw text on every app card.

title: Every send writes the prompt into a persisted queue and removes it again, a queue that never holds anything but can show a jargon 'lane is at capacity' alert.
detail: Expected: No unused queue on the send path; prompt text not written to disk for no purpose. Actual: Two MMKV writes of the prompt per send and an unreachable alert.

title: The three-retry limit and retry backoff never apply, because each retry creates a new message id and the counter is keyed by id.
detail: Expected: Either the limit counts attempts per question, or the dead limit and backoff are removed. Actual: Unlimited immediate retries; dead alert copy.

title: Online detection depends on OS internet validation, so a network that blocks the OS check can make Cloud sends queue forever.
detail: Expected: A device that can reach the AGI API is treated as online. Actual: Possibly treated as offline; every Cloud message is queued and never replayed.

title: Offline, a message in an existing Cloud chat is queued but the first message of a new chat is refused with an alert.
detail: Expected: One offline behaviour, or copy on the composer that says new chats need a connection before typing. Actual: Typed text is kept but the user learns only on Send.

title: The Upgrade chip is built but hidden because mobile v1 has no in-app purchase.
detail: Expected: Hidden until purchases exist. Actual: Hidden.

title: Bank linking, the companion screen and the in-app or system browser choice are built but switched off in v1.
detail: Expected: Hidden in v1. Actual: Hidden; code ships unused.

title: Search finds files and generated images only in chats already loaded on the phone, and ignores the files the server returns.
detail: Expected: File matches the server returns appear in mobile search, as they do in web's search dialog. Actual: Server file matches are dropped; files and images from chats not loaded on the phone are missing from those groups, while the Library screen (server-backed, libraryClient.ts:118) and web's search dialog (GlobalSearchDialog.tsx:682) list them.

title: Attachments added from the voice bar skip the per-message file count and total size checks the composer applies.
detail: Expected: Voice attachments are admitted with the same count and total-size rules as the composer, with the same alert. Actual: A user can stage more files or bytes than one message carries; every file is uploaded through /api/uploads/presign, which counts it against the daily upload limit (presign/route.ts:132 admitAttachmentUpload), then the server leaves the extras out and the chat marks them truncated (chatExecutionStore.ts:3475 onAttachmentsTruncated).

title: The Cloud branch of past-chat retrieval on the phone is never called, and the store privacy notes still describe it.
detail: Expected: No unreachable Cloud retrieval code, and store disclosures that match what the app sends. Actual: Dead code that would also write search history if revived (it omits track=false); disclosure overstates one data flow.

title: The live voice disclosure says audio goes to 'the voice provider' without naming it.
detail: Expected: Likely: the app names who receives the audio and gets an explicit yes. Whether the current App Store rule requires naming the provider was not verified. Actual: The provider is unnamed; Continue serves as the only consent.

title: The Artifacts switch on the phone promises a side preview that the phone does not have.
detail: Expected: Copy that matches the phone: artifacts open full screen. Actual: Web wording on a phone screen.

title: Project search never includes shared projects, and switching to Shared with a search typed shows No matches with no field to clear it.
detail: Expected: Search covers shared projects; changing the filter clears or keeps a visible search. Actual: Type a query under All, switch to Shared with you: the shared list disappears and 'No project matches' shows with no search bar to clear. Under All, shared projects never match a query.

title: Voice settings say only the transcript goes to AGI Cloud, but live voice streams raw audio to a third-party voice provider.
detail: Expected: The settings page states that in Cloud voice conversations audio goes to the voice provider. Actual: It understates what leaves the device.

title: Editing an area of an image from the Library skips the model's edit-support check and always asks for a square 1024x1024 result.
detail: Expected: Same check and the source aspect ratio, as in chat. Actual: Users see a 'Editing the image' toast, then an error for models that cannot edit; wide or tall images come back square.

title: Skill import calls the file picker outside its error handling and uploads without token refresh or a size check.
detail: Expected: Picker and upload failures show the import error; expired tokens refresh; oversize files are refused before upload. Actual: A picker error is silent; an expired token reports 'Could not import this skill'.

title: When a phone edit to a project conflicts with a web edit, the phone's change is dropped without telling the user.
detail: Expected: Field-level merge for independent fields (pin, archive, name), or a visible notice that the change was not kept. Actual: The pin, archive or rename made on the phone silently reverts.

title: The Images page never shows Templates or Ideas tiles, because nothing supplies them.
detail: Expected: Templates and Ideas starter tiles appear, as the feature map and web describe. Actual: Users always see the 'Create an image' empty state; the tab switch, tile grid and pickTile are dead code.

title: Importing a skill whose scan needs review always fails on the phone, because there is no way to acknowledge the scan.
detail: Expected: The phone shows the scan findings and lets the user import anyway, resending with the acknowledgement, as web does. Actual: The same refusal repeats on every attempt.

title: The Library offers a Videos filter that says 'Videos you generate will appear here' although the phone cannot create videos.
detail: Expected: Hide the chip when no video source exists on the phone, or say videos made on the web show here; filter by kind on the server. Actual: An empty Videos view that promises a feature the phone lacks; kind filters can look empty until more pages load.

title: Each Start session tap makes a new requestId, so a retry after a lost response creates a second session and uses another sandbox slot.
detail: Expected: One requestId per sheet opening (per draft), reused on retry, so the server returns the existing session. Actual: A retry provisions a duplicate session; on a 1-2 session plan the user then hits 'Your plan allows N active Code sessions'.

title: The phone offers coding harnesses labelled 'needs your own API key' but has no field for the key, so choosing one always fails.
detail: Expected: Mobile hides or disables runtimes that need a user credential (BYOK is out of scope for the phone). Actual: The user can pick it and gets a refusal after tapping Start.

title: If a new session fails to provision, the task the user typed is never sent and is not put back in the composer.
detail: Expected: On a failed provision the goal is restored into the composer or shown with a retry. Actual: The typed task silently disappears; the user sees a failed session with an empty composer.

title: The Cloud environments screen ships but nothing opens it, and sessions cannot use a saved environment anyway.
detail: Expected: Either a reachable environments feature wired into session creation, or no shipped screen. Actual: Unreachable screen with list and swipe delete that talks to /api/code/environments.

title: Connector connect and AGI Work start replace the server's reason (plan, workspace policy, rate limit) with a generic 'Try again'.
detail: Expected: The alert states why: not on your plan, blocked by your workspace, or try later. Actual: Users retry an action that cannot succeed.

title: A 'Scheduled task needs your approval' push opens the generic Scheduled list instead of the run that is waiting.
detail: Expected: The tap opens that schedule's run history with the Approve and Deny controls. Actual: User must find the schedule and open History by hand.

title: Free users (every public mobile v1 user) cannot create schedules, connect connectors, start AGI Work or open Code sessions; screens show the plan note without a purchase path.
detail: Expected: Per owner decisions: mobile v1 free with no IAP, no subscription sales before 2027-01-01. Actual: As expected; only comped accounts reach these flows on the phone.

title: The Library shows Free accounts storage and download meters with their limits ('X of Y file storage used', 'X of Y file downloads used this month'), against the owner rule that Free sees only Upgrade.
detail: Expected: On Free the Library shows no usage meters or limits (at most an Upgrade action), as Settings > Usage does. Actual: Free users on phone and web see storage and download meters with their caps.

title: A dyslexic font preference is stored and synced but no screen sets it and nothing applies it
detail: Expected: A reachable font choice that changes chat text, or no stored preference. Actual: The value syncs to the cloud and is exported, but the user cannot change it and it has no effect.

title: The phone sizes edit images to the 12,000,000-character contract limit, but the server refuses any request body over 4 MiB.
detail: Expected: The client bounds the whole request under the server's body ceiling, or the route's ceiling matches its contract. Actual: A PNG of about 3 MB or more that is already within 2048 px is sent unshrunk, and several images together can also pass 4 MiB; the server answers 413 before the handler runs.

title: Sign-out says 'Signed out of AGI Cloud' with no warning when the CLI cannot be reached, though the CLI on this machine may still hold a working login.
detail: Expected: Sign-out ends the CLI login too, or says plainly that the CLI is still signed in and how to sign it out. Actual: The editor reports success; depending on token state the CLI either keeps working and is re-adopted, or later fails with 'session ended'.

title: Pending code-block proposals keep their original ranges, so accepting one proposal or any edit above another makes the others fail as stale.
detail: Expected: Accepting one proposal, or typing elsewhere in the file, shifts the remaining proposals and keeps them acceptable. Actual: Accept one by one top-down and every later proposal is refused; highlighted lines drift off the code they describe.

title: Batch accept and reject (CodeLens and two commands) can never appear because no caller creates a batch.
detail: Expected: Either a producer sets batchId and confidence, or the code is removed. Actual: Unreachable UI and commands.

title: Restore Rejected Diffs only brings back the most recent rejection; earlier rejected proposals are lost without notice.
detail: Expected: Restore returns every change rejected in this session, or the copy says it restores the last rejection. Actual: Reject A, then reject B: Restore brings back only B.

title: Image attachment thumbnails use blob: URLs that the chat panel's content security policy blocks, so chips show a broken image.
detail: Expected: A thumbnail of the pasted screenshot, or a file icon. Actual: A broken-image glyph in each image chip.

title: Dropping more than eight files attaches the first eight and silently ignores the rest.
detail: Expected: A notice that only eight files can be attached at once. Actual: Files nine and later vanish with no message.

title: The main sign-in path (through the CLI) uses the local 2.5 second browser-open timeout and never says the page opens on your own computer.
detail: Expected: Both paths use deviceAuthorizationOpenTimeoutMs(remoteName) and describeDeviceAuthorizationBrowser. Actual: In SSH, WSL and container windows users usually get the generic 'Enter code at URL' warning without the remote explanation the feature row claims.

title: Cancelling sign-in leaves the CLI's device login pending because the extension never calls account/login/cancel.
detail: Expected: Cancel stops the CLI login so a later browser approval does not sign the machine in. Actual: Approving the page after cancelling still signs the CLI in, and the editor adopts it.

title: Check the CLI (/doctor) reports success for a CLI the runtime will refuse as too old.
detail: Expected: The check says the version is below the minimum and how to update. Actual: Success message, then chat fails with a version error.

title: The CLI installer and release check always use agiworkforce.com, ignoring the configured AGI origin.
detail: Expected: Installer and release feed follow the configured origin. Actual: A staging-configured editor checks and installs from production.

title: Palette commands for compact, status, export and checkpoints always act on the sidebar chat, even when an editor-tab chat is focused.
detail: Expected: The palette command acts on the focused chat panel. Actual: Running Code: Summarize Session from an editor chat tab compacts the sidebar session or says there is none.

title: The status bar credit estimate and billed credits show for every plan, while Account & Usage hides session meters on Free.
detail: Expected: Free users see no credit meter, consistent with the Free usage rule. Actual: Free users who make managed utility requests see credit figures in the status bar breakdown.

title: When the account comes only from the CLI, Account & Usage shows usage and billing rows without checking for Free.
detail: Expected: Free accounts see only Upgrade in every branch. Actual: A Free CLI account sees usage and billing links and no Upgrade.

title: The chat webview accepts any window message without checking its source.
detail: Expected: Defense in depth: ignore messages whose event.source is not the parent window. Actual: No check.

title: The model dashboard's inline style attributes are blocked by its own content security policy.
detail: Expected: Centered, muted empty-state text. Actual: Unstyled text.

title: Code-block Apply status strings are hard-coded English.
detail: Expected: Strings come from the vscode locale catalog. Actual: English in every locale.

title: One server error while polling ends the fallback sign-in, and an unreadable success response throws out of the progress notification.
detail: Expected: Transient 5xx answers are retried like network errors until the grant expires. Actual: A single 502 from the edge ends sign-in and asks the user to start again.

title: On Windows the CLI lookup accepts agi.cmd, which Node cannot spawn without a shell.
detail: Expected: Only executables that can be spawned are accepted. Actual: A stray agi.cmd is chosen and fails with an unclear spawn error.

title: The project chosen for chat survives sign-out, so the next account on this workspace sends the previous account's project id and instructions with every turn.
detail: Expected: Signing out, or signing in as another account, clears the active project. Actual: After an account switch the composer still shows the old project and turns carry its id and instructions.

title: A cloud-task link may name a branch that starts with a dash, which is then passed to git checkout as an option.
detail: Expected: Branch names starting with '-' are rejected when the link is parsed. Actual: A crafted link can ask git to run checkout with an option such as -f, which discards local changes, after two prompts that show the odd branch name.

title: Installing a skill from a folder has no trust confirmation, unlike plugins, MCP servers and hooks.
detail: Expected: The same 'runs on this computer with your permissions' confirmation before a skill is installed. Actual: One click in a file dialog installs it.

title: /status shows 'Not signed in' whenever the CLI cannot answer, even when the editor holds its own session.
detail: Expected: The row uses resolveAccountPresence (CLI, then the editor's own token). Actual: Signed-in users see Not signed in.
