title: Git Commit commits every tracked change without showing which files go in.
detail: Expected: Show the files that will be committed, or commit only staged changes. Actual: Unrelated local edits are committed together with the agent's.

title: Continue in the Cloud makes a new requestId on every attempt, so running it again after a timeout or the misleading failure message starts a second session.
detail: Expected: One key per hand-off, reused when the user repeats the same hand-off, so the server returns the existing session. Actual: Each rerun provisions another sandbox and can hit 'Your plan allows N active Code sessions'.

title: The Security pane shows Trusted contact · Not configured although there is no way to configure one.
detail: Expected: Either no row, or plain copy that the feature is not offered. Actual: Users look for a setup control that does not exist.

title: Unused pricing strings that contradict current policy ship in every locale bundle.
detail: Expected: Locale files carry only live, accurate strings. Actual: Dead, contradictory copy is bundled and can be revived by mistake.

title: Choosing Spanish translates only menus, navigation and pricing; about 24 of 1,029 web components use translations.
detail: Expected: Documented partial scope (as now). Actual: Most of the product stays English after switching.

title: 'Share answer' creates no link: it hands plain text to the OS share sheet or, where that API is missing, silently does the same as Copy.
detail: Expected: A share action produces a viewable link (as chat sharing does via /api/share), or the item is labelled Copy text / Share text. Actual: No link; desktop browsers without Web Share get a duplicate Copy button, and formatting, citations and images are dropped.

title: The Edit button on your own message stays enabled while a reply streams, and clicking it does nothing.
detail: Expected: Edit is disabled with a tooltip while a reply runs, like Retry. Actual: Click is ignored silently.

title: 'Sent at' shows only the hour and minute, so messages from earlier days show no date unless you hover.
detail: Expected: Show the date when the message is not from today. Actual: 'Sent at 10:42' for a message from last month.

title: Search does not escape LIKE wildcards, so a query containing % or _ matches unrelated chats.
detail: Expected: Literal search for the characters typed. Actual: Searching '_' or '100%' returns wildcard matches.

title: Sharing right after stopping an answer before any text appeared can be refused as 'changes not saved yet', because the stored row holds a zero-width placeholder the local row lacks.
detail: Expected: An empty stopped answer matches its stored row and the chat shares. Actual: Likely refusal until reload. Not closed: whether the server's own snapshot (content '') wins the row over the client save.

title: Screen capture exists in the shared attachment menu but is not offered in the web composer.
detail: Expected: Owner decides whether web should offer it. Actual: Not on web.

title: 'Report this response' files every report as 'harmful' in one click, with no reason picker, note or confirmation, though the backend takes six categories and mobile asks for one.
detail: Expected: A small dialog asks why (category plus optional note) before sending, as on mobile and in the leaders. Actual: One accidental click files a 'harmful' report with no context.

title: With the message-variants kill switch on, regenerating an earlier answer deletes it and every later message without asking.
detail: Expected: Any regenerate that will delete later turns asks first and names how many, as the user-retry path does. Actual: Later turns are deleted once the new answer commits, without a prompt.

title: Pinning a message only draws a small icon next to it; there is no list of pinned messages and no way to jump to them, and the icon is hidden from screen readers.
detail: Expected: Pinned messages can be found again (a list in the header or a search filter), and the badge has an accessible label. Actual: A pin is a decoration on one bubble in a long, virtualised transcript.

title: A grouped citation chip ('site +2') opens only the first source; the other sources appear in a hover tooltip as plain text that cannot be clicked, focused or opened on touch.
detail: Expected: Each grouped source can be opened by mouse, keyboard and touch (a popover with links, as in the leaders). Actual: Sources 2..n of a group are reachable only through the separate Sources panel.

title: Mark as unread is stored only in this browser, so it does not follow the user to other devices or apps; the 'Better' rating overstates it.
detail: Expected: An owner decision: keep it per device, or add a server column so web, desktop and mobile agree. Actual: Per-browser only.

title: Three feature-map rows describe the code wrongly: Send with Enter already exists, a notification offer already shows during long tasks, and row 107 points at a render-crash boundary instead of the turn failure notice.
detail: Expected: The comparison reflects the code. Actual: Row 52 is scored Missing and rows 105 and 107 cite the wrong evidence.

title: There is no way to take a chat out of a project on web: Move to project lists only projects and nothing sends projectId null.
detail: Expected: A 'Remove from project' choice, as ChatGPT offers. Actual: A chat moved into a project by mistake can only be moved to another project or deleted.

title: The greeting first shows the user's name and then removes it for someone who switched names off, and for others it renders nameless then pops the name in.
detail: Expected: An opted-out user never sees their name; the headline waits until the name source is settled. Actual: Name appears for a fetch round trip, then disappears; or the nameless variant shows and is replaced.

title: The desktop download link exists only in WebAppShell's footer; the main /chat page hand-builds its own footer without it.
detail: Expected: One footer component on every signed-in page; download link hidden inside the desktop host. Actual: Users on /chat, where they spend most time, never see Get apps; two footers drift.

title: The command palette's model list offers every Max-tier chat model and a New AGI Work action to every account, ignoring the plan locks the composer picker shows.
detail: Expected: The palette lists the same entitled models as the picker (locked ones marked) and hides Work for plans without it. Actual: A Free user can select a Max-only model from the palette; what the next send does was not traced (server refusal or reroute suspected). New AGI Work silently opens a normal chat.

title: The running dot reflects only streams in this browser tab, so a Work task running on the server shows no dot after a reload or on another device.
detail: Expected: A server-side running run marks its row, as the needs_you flag already does. Actual: After reload, a long Work task looks idle until it finishes or needs input.

title: Search on /chat/chats filters only the titles already loaded, then says 'Nothing matches' even when older chats would match.
detail: Expected: Search covers all chats (or says it searched only loaded ones); bulk archive confirms with Undo. Actual: Older matching chats are reported as absent; archived rows vanish silently.

title: Starting a study session creates the conversation first, and if the study start call fails the empty titled conversation is left behind.
detail: Expected: A failed start leaves no stray chat, or reuses the one already created. Actual: Each failed attempt adds an empty 'Study: <topic>' chat to the sidebar.

title: On AGI Work plans a project scope and Chat mode cannot coexist on /chat: picking a project switches to Work and choosing Chat removes the project.
detail: Expected: Paid users can start an ordinary chat inside a project, as Free users can. Actual: Every paid project chat started from /chat is a Work task (autonomy, approvals).

title: 'Manage connectors' and 'Browse connectors' in the plus menu are two rows that open the same settings section.
detail: Expected: Browse opens the connector directory (or one row is removed). Actual: Two identical destinations under different names.

title: The Copy button on a message calls the clipboard without a try/catch, so a denied or unavailable clipboard fails with no message.
detail: Expected: Copy failure shows 'Could not copy' like the other copy controls. Actual: Nothing happens and an unhandled rejection is logged.

title: Read aloud speaks the raw markdown source, so every chart, card, checklist or other answer block is read as 'code block omitted' and inline code is skipped mid-sentence.
detail: Expected: Read aloud uses the same plain-text rendering as Copy, reading block contents and inline code. Actual: 'Run to install' for 'Run `npm i` to install'; a card answer is read as repeated 'code block omitted'.

title: The slider block has no step, so fractional ranges snap to whole numbers, and its value readout is not announced.
detail: Expected: Step derived from the values' precision; readout exposed as output; feature copy matches what controls do. Actual: Decimal sliders jump between integers; screen readers miss the readout.

title: The sidebar's Organize chats choice is plain component state, so it resets to By project on every reload and when moving between /chat and other pages.
detail: Expected: The choice persists like other sidebar preferences (hiddenNavIds are in the settings store). Actual: Users who pick 'In one list' lose it on the next navigation.

title: Three rows in this unit describe the code wrongly.
detail: Expected: Rows match the implementation. Actual: Ratings rest on code paths users do not reach or that behave differently.

title: The project page composer takes whatever Chat or Work mode was last set on the /chat home composer and offers no switch to change it.
detail: Expected: The project composer shows the mode it will send and lets the user change it, or uses its own default. Actual: A user who left /chat in Work sends a Work task from the project page with no way to choose Chat there.

title: The ```citation answer block renders its url as a raw link, skipping the URL safety transform and new-tab handling every other answer link gets.
detail: Expected: Citation links get the same protocol allowlist, tracking-param stripping and new-tab behaviour as markdown links. Actual: Any scheme is linked; clicking replaces the chat page.

title: Ctrl/Cmd+B flips a hidden preference when the sidebar is in rail or drawer mode, so it does nothing visible and the sidebar comes back in the opposite state later.
detail: Expected: The key does what the toggle button does in the current mode (open the drawer in rail/drawer mode). Actual: No visible change; after closing the panel the sidebar is collapsed or expanded contrary to what the user last saw.

title: The web image picker keeps its own aspect ratio table that has drifted from the catalog and the server: Gemini's 1:4, 4:1, 1:8 and 8:1 are missing and 9:21 is listed but never offered.
detail: Expected: One owner for per-API aspect ratios (AGENTS.md sections 3 and 4); the web picker reads the catalog helper. Actual: Three tables; the web offers fewer ratios than the server accepts and carries a dead 9:21 option.

title: The heavy-model usage warning exists only as a hover tooltip on a non-focusable span, so keyboard, screen reader and touch users never get it.
detail: Expected: The warning is visible in the row (guidance line or badge) or announced in its accessible name, as the degraded and deprecation notes are. Actual: Only a mouse hover reveals it.

title: Resume on a paused or failed research run reports success and silently does nothing when another reply is streaming.
detail: Expected: Resume is disabled while another reply streams, or shows why it did not start, and the handler returns false when nothing was sent. Actual: The click does nothing and gives no feedback.

title: A microphone that another app is using (NotReadableError) is reported as 'The voice connection could not be established' instead of a microphone problem.
detail: Expected: A busy or failing microphone says so and suggests closing the other app or choosing another microphone. Actual: The user is told the connection failed and may retry a network problem that does not exist.

title: Web voice has no push-to-talk while the phone app offers it in voice settings.
detail: Expected: Same voice input modes across surfaces, or a recorded deviation. Actual: Web is hands-free only.

title: Confirmed absent: search location, restaurant booking, audio and video attachments, and GIF image output; no half-built code found.
detail: Expected: Owner decides whether to build these. Actual: Absent as the comparison says.

title: Changing the voice in the settings opened during a live voice session does nothing to that session and nothing says it applies next time.
detail: Expected: The voice picker says the new voice starts with the next session, or the session restarts with it. Actual: The picker shows the new voice while the old voice keeps speaking.

title: The public /pair page tells people to scan a pairing QR code with the phone app, which has no pairing screen in v1.
detail: Expected: While Remote Control is hidden on the phone, /pair says pairing is not available yet (or the route is not linked), instead of giving steps. Actual: The page gives step-by-step pairing instructions that cannot be completed on any released phone build.

title: The Artifacts and Inline visualizations switches never appear, and the prompt code that would honour them has no caller.
detail: Expected: Either wire the request path to read capabilities.artifacts and inlineVisualizations into capabilityPreferences and report the switches, or remove the unused branches until the switches ship. Actual: Users see only Cloud code execution and Tool access. The comparison row claims Artifacts and Inline visualizations switches that do not render; the prompt branches are dead in production.

title: Versions made by hand edits live only in this browser: the server records them but nothing reads them back, so that history is gone on another device or after signing out.
detail: Expected: Version history, restore and Show changes follow the account like the artifact itself, since the server already keeps the versions. Actual: On a second device, in Desktop, or after sign-out, in-panel edits collapse to the latest content; earlier hand-edited versions cannot be restored or diffed.

title: Turning memory off for one chat is stored only in this browser, so the same chat uses memory again on another device or after signing out.
detail: Expected: A per-chat memory choice is saved with the conversation so every device and surface honours it, like the chat's project, model and draft. Actual: The chat silently reads and writes memory when continued on the phone, in Desktop, in another browser, or after sign-out and sign-in.

title: Shared-project copy says only the owner can add or remove sources, but members with Can edit can.
detail: Expected: Copy says the owner or people with edit access can add sources, and the help article mentions Can edit. Actual: Viewers are told to ask only the owner; editors reading the help think they cannot add sources.

title: Gmail draft actions and Save to Google Docs, Drive and OneDrive exist but stay hidden behind the unreleased connectors switch.
detail: Expected: Stays hidden until the connectors are released (owner decision recorded in policy-versions.json). Actual: Backend and menu code ship dark; rows 12 and 13 read Missing to users.

title: AI calls from published apps are fully routed but switched off by AGI_ARTIFACT_AI_ENABLED until a security review passes.
detail: Expected: Hidden until the review passes. Actual: Row 20 reads Missing; code is present and dark.

title: The sidebar offers Rename, Pin and Delete on projects shared with you, which the server refuses for non-owners.
detail: Expected: Rows for shared projects show only open, new chat and, for editors, settings. Actual: Members see Delete project and Pin; choosing them flashes the row away and back with an error.

title: Edit with AI on a selection asks the model to rewrite the whole artifact and only instructs it to keep the rest; nothing checks that it did.
detail: Expected: A targeted replace of the selected range, or a check that unselected text is unchanged before the result becomes the next version. Actual: Long documents are regenerated in full, costing output tokens, and the model can alter or truncate other sections.

title: When the in-chat Connect link is refused for plan, policy, unconfirmed email or coming soon, the user is sent back with no message.
detail: Expected: The user sees why (upgrade needed, admin blocked it, confirm your email, coming soon). Actual: The page reloads and nothing happens.

title: The Health space appears when the HealthEx OAuth app is configured, although that connector is not released and cannot be connected.
detail: Expected: The Health space shows only when its connector can actually be connected. Actual: If the OAuth app is configured in production, US users see a Health space whose main action fails.

title: The Your computer page asks users to pair Desktop, which is marked Coming soon.
detail: Expected: Hide the page, or say Desktop is coming soon instead of giving pairing steps. Actual: Users can reach a flow they cannot complete.

title: A Finances page and live bank-account routes exist with no navigation entry and a switched-off connector.
detail: Expected: Either finish and release it, or remove the page and routes until the owner decides. Actual: Reachable only by URL; connecting a bank is refused as coming soon.

title: Start Work is offered on artifacts to plans without Work, and the request is silently sent as an ordinary chat.
detail: Expected: Hide the item, or show the Work upgrade message, when the plan lacks agi_work. Actual: The control looks like it starts Work but does not.

title: The new-chat connector suggestion card is shown to plans that cannot use connectors.
detail: Expected: Free accounts do not get a 'connect your apps' prompt, or the card says connectors need a paid plan. Actual: Free users are sent to a settings pane that refuses the connection.

title: A Cloud Code turn that outlasts the request is shown on web as a failed turn with Retry, although it is still running.
detail: Expected: A still-running turn stays shown as running and is followed until it settles, as on mobile. Actual: Traced in code, not run: the record becomes an error (carrying the server's 'still running' text) with Retry and the prompt restored; the finished turn shows only after the session is reopened, beside the stale error record, which has no turnId to merge on (620-627).

title: The background forwards any message type it does not name to any tab's content script under a cross-tab default, so an unapproved tab's page HTML can be read through it.
detail: Expected: Unknown message types are rejected; cross-tab page reads exist only as explicit, origin-authorized cases. Actual: A content script on an approved site, if its renderer is compromised, can ask for the HTML, text or accessibility tree of any other tab, including blocked and banking tabs. No runtime sender in product code needs the default branch.
